President Donald J. Trump is systematically dismantling the bloodthirsty Tren de Aragua gang that Biden’s open borders allowed to pour into American communities. The Trump Administration has launched the largest federal campaign against transnational crime in U.S. history — identifying, arresting, and removing these vicious foreign criminals and driving violent crime down nationwide.

The Washington Examiner highlights the Trump Administration’s latest effort:

“The Trump administration has waged an aggressive campaign against Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, whose members entered the United States through the vulnerable U.S.-Mexico border during the Biden administration.

The White House, Department of Homeland Security, and Department of Justice launched Homeland Security Task Forces in 2025 with the goal of identifying, finding, and removing criminal rings and terrorist organizations embedded in U.S. communities, particularly Tren de Aragua.

It is the largest campaign against transnational crime that the government has undertaken in history and one of the reasons violent crime rates overall have dropped precipitously nationwide since 2025…

Task force data publicly released for the first time to the Washington Examiner showed law enforcement arrested 1,296 Tren de Aragua gang members between Jan. 20, 2025, and Oct. 8, 2026, and charged nearly 350 Tren de Aragua members and associates with federal crimes.”

Today, President Donald J. Trump heads to Montana for a stop in Kalispell. He arrives with a proven record of America First policies that put Montana workers, families, seniors, and communities first — delivering historic tax relief, unleashing private investment and job growth, securing energy dominance, building critical minerals independence, and protecting public lands and rural communities.

Delivering Tax Relief for Hardworking Montanans

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting money back in the pockets of Montana workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 200,000 Montana seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: Montana taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,304 in 2026.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 20,000 Montana jobs, $4 billion in state GDP, and $2 billion in workers’ wages.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare

President Trump is bolstering access to care in Montana’s rural and frontier communities.

  • Rural Health Investments: Montana secured $233 million in first-year Rural Health Transformation Program funding from the Working Families Tax Cuts — the fourth-highest award among all states.
  • Rural EMS: The Trump Administration announced $8.7 million in September 2026 from the Rural Health Transformation Program for new ambulances and lifesaving equipment at 79 rural Montana EMS agencies, including three tribal governments.
  • Behavioral Health: Montana secured federal approval in May 2026 to stand up certified community behavioral health clinics at roughly 20 sites statewide, replacing short-term grants with permanent funding.

Growing Montana’s Manufacturing Base

President Trump’s pro-growth agenda is driving private investment and job creation across the state.

  • Janicki Industries selected Great Falls for an $800 million advanced manufacturing campus, creating more than 1,000 jobs within five years and more than 2,000 jobs at completion.
  • Montana ranked ninth in the nation for job growth during the first year of President Trump’s second term.
  • Under Republican leadership, Montana’s unemployment rate stood at 3.2% in August — well below the national average and ranking among the lowest in the country.

Driving American Energy Dominance

President Trump’s energy dominance agenda has reversed the previous Administration’s restrictions and unlocked major coal development that supports high-paying jobs and reliable power.

  • Spring Creek Mine (Big Horn County): In March 2025, the Department of the Interior approved an expansion that extends the mine’s operating life by 16 years, enables production of 39.9 million tons of coal, and supports hundreds of jobs.
  • Rosebud Mine (Rosebud and Treasure counties): Interior approved an expansion that recovers 33.75 million tons of federal coal, extends operations through 2039, supports more than 300 high-paying jobs, and supplies the Colstrip and Rosebud power plants, which together generate 1,500 megawatts of electricity.
  • Bull Mountains Mine: Interior approved a mining plan modification that authorizes 22.8 million tons of federal coal and 34.5 million tons of adjacent non-federal coal, extends the mine by up to nine years, supports more than 250 jobs, and enables significant exports to U.S. allies.

Building America’s Critical Minerals Supply Chain

President Trump is restoring domestic production of critical minerals and ending reliance on foreign adversaries.

  • United States Antimony Corporation (USAC) has earned millions in Department of War grant milestones for its Thompson Falls smelter expansion under a $27 million Defense Production Act award.
  • USAC resumed mining at Stibnite Hill and is processing ore at its newly acquired Radersburg mill, restoring domestic antimony production for the first time in decades.
  • Montana antimony is refilling the National Defense Stockpile under a five-year, $245 million contract with the Defense Logistics Agency.

Returning Control of Lands and Water to Montanans

President Trump is putting decision-making back in the hands of Montanans while delivering critical infrastructure.

  • Grizzly Bears: The Fish and Wildlife Service proposed a rule in July 2026 giving Montana and other Western states greater flexibility to manage grizzlies in the Yellowstone ecosystem and other recovery areas where populations have met or exceeded recovery benchmarks, while maintaining Endangered Species Act protections.
  • Fort Peck Water: President Trump signed the Fort Peck rural water reauthorization in September 2026, keeping clean water construction on schedule for the Fort Peck Reservation and Roosevelt, Sheridan, Valley, and Daniels counties.
  • Crow Tribe Water Rights: Congress passed the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act in September 2026 and sent it to President Trump’s desk, giving the tribe flexibility to finish its water system and hydropower project.

Rebuilding America’s Nuclear Deterrent at Malmstrom AFB

President Trump is modernizing the land-based leg of the nuclear triad in Montana.

  • The Air Force and Army Corps of Engineers broke ground in May 2026 on a $26 million commercial entrance facility that clears the way for nearly $1 billion in Sentinel construction work at Malmstrom.
  • Work is advancing on surveying and preparing sites across central Montana’s missile fields to replace the aging Minuteman III with the new Sentinel ICBM.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering America First policies that put Montana first: lower taxes, major private investment, energy dominance, a secure critical minerals supply chain, safer communities, and critical infrastructure. Montanans face a clear choice between continuing this progress or returning to the higher taxes, energy restrictions, and failed policies of the past.

Today, President Donald J. Trump returns to the Grand Canyon State for a visit to Bullhead City. He arrives with a clear record of America First results that put Arizona workers, families, seniors, and communities first — delivering tax relief, unleashing major private investment, ending the Biden-era border crisis, driving down violent crime, and securing Arizona’s critical water resources.

Delivering Tax Relief for Hardworking Arizonans

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are delivering direct relief to Arizona workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 1.3 million Arizona seniors benefit from the new senior deduction.
  • Bigger Refunds: Arizona taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,659 in 2026.
  • Rural Health Investments: Arizona secured $167 million in first-year Rural Health Transformation Program funding.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 119,000 Arizona jobs, $22 billion in state GDP, and $11 billion in workers’ wages.

Unleashing an Investment Boom in Arizona

President Trump’s agenda of tax cuts, energy dominance, secure borders, and pro-growth policies has attracted major private capital and high-quality jobs to Arizona.

  • Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company is expanding advanced semiconductor manufacturing at its Phoenix facility with a $200 billion investment.
  • EVelution Energy is building an $850 million cobalt processing facility in Yuma County, creating 3,300 jobs.
  • Amkor Technology is constructing a $2 billion semiconductor packaging and test facility in Peoria, creating 2,200 jobs.
  • Hadrian is establishing a $200 million large-scale manufacturing and software hub in Mesa, creating 350 jobs.
  • Cyclic Materials is developing its first $20 million commercial facility in Mesa.

Securing the Southern Border

President Trump ended the Biden-era border crisis and restored control at the southern border.

  • The Trump Administration has not released a single illegal alien into the country at the border for 16 consecutive months.
  • Southern border apprehensions in August were 94% lower than the monthly average under Biden.
  • Refugee admissions in the first ten months of this fiscal year are down almost 90% from 2024.
  • The Working Families Tax Cuts allocated $46.5 billion to complete the border wall.
  • Fentanyl and other drug trafficking are down, with CBP seizing 73% more drugs this fiscal year through August than in the same period of FY 2024, and 61% more than the average for the same period over the prior four years.
  • The Trump Administration transferred 285 acres of public land in Yuma County along the U.S.-Mexico border to the Department of the Navy to establish a National Defense Area in direct support of border security operations.

Making Safer Streets Across Arizona

Violent crime is falling as President Trump’s law-and-order agenda delivers real results for Arizona communities.

  • Violent crime fell 13% statewide last year, including a 13% drop in homicides, an 11% drop in aggravated assaults, a 24% drop in robberies, and a 10% drop in sexual assaults.
  • In Mesa, homicides fell 33% and rapes fell 15% in the first half of this year compared with the same period last year.
  • In Phoenix, homicides fell 22% and robberies fell 19% in the first half of this year compared with the same period last year.
  • In Tucson, homicides fell 24% and robberies fell 10% in the first half of this year compared with the same period last year.

Protecting Arizona’s Water Resources

The Trump Administration is making targeted investments to strengthen Arizona’s water supply and long-term resilience.

  • In July 2025, the Bureau of Reclamation announced a $179 million investment to design and construct the North Gateway Advanced Water Purification Facility in Phoenix.
  • In May 2025, the Trump Administration finalized 18 short-term System Conservation Implementation agreements with water entitlement holders in Arizona and California to increase conservation of Colorado River System water.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering America First policies that put Arizona first: lower taxes, major private investment, a secure border, safer communities, and critical water infrastructure. Arizonans face a clear choice between continuing this progress, or returning to the higher taxes, energy restrictions, and open borders policies of the past.

Today, President Donald J. Trump travels to Alaska. He returns to the Last Frontier with a proven record of results that put Alaskans first: lower taxes, responsible development of the state’s vast energy and mineral resources, safer communities, strong support for fisheries, and major investments that create jobs and reinforce America’s Arctic security.

Tax Relief That Puts Money Back in Alaskans’ Pockets

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are delivering direct relief to Alaska workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Tips: Approximately 14,000 Alaska workers no longer pay federal income taxes on tips.
  • No Tax on Social Security: About 100,000 Alaska seniors benefit from the new senior deduction.
  • Bigger Refunds: Alaska taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,690 in 2026.
  • Rural Health Investments: Alaska secured about $272 million in first-year Rural Health Transformation Program funding.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 11,000 Alaska jobs, $2 billion in state GDP, and $1 billion in workers’ wages.

Unleashing Alaska’s Energy, Minerals, and Economic Potential

President Trump is reversing years of restrictions, unlocking responsible development of Alaska’s oil, gas, and critical minerals.

  • In October 2026, the Trump Administration secured $150 million in Defense Production Act funding for a major new power line that will lower energy costs for 75% of Alaskans.
  • In September 2026, President Trump unveiled a $200 billion South Korean investment in U.S. energy that includes $54 billion to construct a new natural gas pipeline in Alaska.
  • In December 2025, the Trump Administration reopened nearly 82% of the National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska to oil and gas leasing.
  • In October 2025, the Trump Administration opened 1.56 million acres of the Coastal Plain to oil and gas leasing, reversing Biden-era restrictions.
  • In October 2025, President Trump approved the Ambler Road Project, providing essential access to the Ambler Mining District’s large deposits of copper, cobalt, gallium, germanium, and other critical minerals.
  • In June 2025, the Trump Administration advanced plans to open an additional seven million federally managed acres on the North Slope to new oil development.
  • In January 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order directing federal agencies to prioritize development of Alaska’s oil, gas, minerals, and other natural resources.

Protecting Alaska’s Communities, Fisheries, and Veterans

President Trump has moved quickly to restore historic names, support Alaska’s vital fishing industry, and expand care for the state’s veterans.

  • On his first day in office, President Trump restored the name Mount McKinley, reversing the Obama Administration’s 2015 change and returning the designation that stood from 1917.
  • The Trump Administration ensured Alaska groundfish fisheries opened on time, protecting a total value of $301.1 million for Gulf of Alaska fisheries and $2.64 billion for Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands fisheries.
  • The Trump Administration implemented regulatory and data collection reforms that allowed the timely opening of the Alaska halibut fishery.
  • The Department of Veterans Affairs awarded over $4 million in grants to community organizations supporting Alaska veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
  • In September 2026, the VA opened a new walk-in clinic at the Colonel Mary Louise Rasmuson Campus in Anchorage.
  • The Trump Administration delivered funding for critical infrastructure upgrades at the Alaska VA Healthcare System as part of a record $4.8 billion in nationwide VA spending.

A Military Construction Boom Across Alaska

President Trump and Republicans in Congress have directed major new investments into Alaska’s bases, creating jobs and modernizing facilities that strengthen U.S. security in the Arctic.

  • President Trump signed the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026, which included:
    • $208 million for new barracks at Fort Wainwright in Fairbanks.
    • $46 million for a base supply complex at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER) in Anchorage.
    • $152 million for the next phase of the Joint Integrated Test and Training Center at JBER.
    • $45 million to complete the Air Force runway extension at JBER.
    • $6.7 million to finish planning and design for a permanent party dormitory at Eielson Air Force Base.
    • $7.7 million to begin planning and design for a new Army dining facility at Fort Wainwright.
  • President Trump signed the FY 2026 National Defense Authorization Act, which delivered additional Alaska funding, including:
    • $82 million for the Air Force Joint Integrated Test & Training Center at JBER.
    • $80 million for upgraded Army barracks at Fort Wainwright.
    • $46 million for an Army Reserve Base Supply Complex at JBER.
    • $46 million for an Army Reserve Maintenance Facility at JBER.
    • $15 million for a Base Civil Engineering Pavements and Grounds Facility for the Alaska Air National Guard at Eielson.
    • $13.2 million for design of an Air Force Consolidated Munitions Complex at Eielson.
    • $8 million for design of an Army dining facility at Fort Wainwright.
    • $1.75 million for design of an Air Force Coal Thaw Shed Addition at Eielson.
  • The FY 2027 NDAA, which has passed the House, includes $2.6 billion for Alaska and launches the multi-year, $7 billion “Fighter Town USA” recapitalization at JBER. The project will construct 26 modern facilities, position JBER as one of the most strategically important bases in the world, create up to 4,000 private-sector jobs, and bring additional military personnel and families to Alaska.

Safer Streets Across Alaska

Violent crime is falling in Alaska as President Trump’s law-and-order agenda delivers results for Alaska communities.

  • The statewide murder rate fell 13% last year.
  • Juneau recorded a 6% decline in total criminal offenses last year.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering America First policies that put Alaska first: lower taxes, responsible resource development, safer communities, and major investments in the state’s military and economic future. Alaskans face a clear choice between continuing this progress, or returning to the higher taxes, energy restrictions, and open border policies of the past.

Today, Katie Zacharia delivered a commanding inaugural press briefing as the 37th White House Press Secretary.   • Katie opened the briefing with clear purpose: “I am so honored to work for President Trump and the American people as the new White House Press Secretary. I want to thank President Trump for his trust that he has placed in me. I have wanted to work for him for a very long time.” (Watch)

President Donald J. Trump is delivering on his promise to the American worker: build it here, power it here, and put paychecks back in the communities Washington left behind. In a matter of weeks, President Trump has locked in a run of steel, nuclear, gas, shipbuilding, and medical manufacturing commitments that will hire American workers and strengthen American security.

  • President Trump announced that Mesabi Metallics will build a $15 billion steel complex in Iowa — the largest steel plant ever built in the United States. Fed by American iron ore and driven by the Trump Administration’s steel tariffs, the fully integrated mine-to-mill complex will create 1,750 new, permanent jobs, support up to 6,000 construction jobs, and generate an estimated $95 billion in economic output.
  • President Trump and Anduril announced Arsenal-2, the biggest new American shipyard push since World War II, now moving forward in Maryland. The yard will produce critical Virginia-class components and large assemblies, create about 3,100 direct jobs, and support more than 11,000 indirect jobs. Anduril is investing $3.7 billion in private capital; the Navy is putting up to $2.9 billion behind it as part of the Trump Administration’s push to reshore America’s defense industrial base.
  • President Trump unveiled a South Korean energy investment package of up to $200 billion in the United States. The package includes as much as $120 billion to build eight large-scale nuclear plants, $54 billion tied to the Alaska LNG pipeline, and $22.3 billion for a six-gigawatt natural gas power facility in Texas.
  • Vice President Vance announced that the Department of Energy will invest $150 million to advance a major new transmission line in Alaska. The project includes 223 miles linking the Beluga power station on the southern coast with Healy in the Interior, a corridor serving ports and nearly three-quarters of the state’s population.
  • Becton Dickinson announced a $19 billion U.S. investment under a landmark partnership with the Trump Administration, including $3 billion to expand American manufacturing. BD will produce 100% of the needles it sells in America with American-made steel and expand domestic output of essential products.
  • AstraZeneca announced a $1 billion investment in Massachusetts under the $50 billion investment commitment it made in its Most Favored Nation agreement with the Trump Administration. The company is expanding its domestic research and manufacturing operation and growing its domestic workforce.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Today at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit, President Donald J. Trump presented National Medals of Science and National Medals of Technology and Innovation, our nation’s highest honors for exemplary achievement and leadership in science and technology, to six of America’s greatest living innovators.
 
Since 1963, the President of the United States has bestowed the National Medal of Science on those deserving of special recognition for their outstanding contributions to science in service of the United States. Since it was first awarded in 1985, the National Medal of Technology and Innovation has recognized American innovators whose vision, intellect, creativity, and determination have strengthened America’s economy and improved our quality of life.

President Trump is committed to restoring U.S. global scientific and technological leadership for a New Golden Age, from harnessing super intelligence for scientific discovery to ushering in a nuclear renaissance; from ensuring American space superiority to strengthening America’s quantum advantage.

These medalists have pioneered breakthroughs in science and engineering for the new age of super intelligence, from fundamental advances in general-purpose parallel computing and semiconductor design to engineering and business leadership in building the foundations of hyperscale infrastructure in the U.S., around the world, and even into space. Their work has advanced American global technology leadership for the 21st Century and laid the foundation for a new Golden Age of Science.

The recipients are listed below. 

Recipients of the National Medal of Science

  • Elon Musk – “For engineering achievements of extraordinary ambition and scale that have pushed the frontiers of space exploration, intelligent systems, communications, and beyond, renewing American technological leadership and opening a new chapter in American manufacturing.”
  • Sergey Brin – “For the development of foundational algorithms for information retrieval and data processing that revolutionized how the world accesses information across science, commerce, and in the course of everyday life.” 
  • Jensen Huang – “For advancing the graphics processing unit into a general-purpose computing architecture through innovations in processor design and software, transforming massively parallel computation and powering breakthroughs in scientific computing and super intelligence.”
  • Lisa Su – “For a lifetime of leadership in semiconductor engineering and high-performance computing through innovations in processor architecture and chiplet-based integration that powered the world’s first exascale supercomputer and opened new frontiers in computational performance.”

Recipients of the National Medal of Technology and Innovation

  • Michael Dell – “For advancing a vision of widespread adoption of personal and enterprise computing; for his technical and business management skills building a worldwide technology company; and for his support for the next generation of American scientists, engineers, and technologists.”
  • Satya Nadella – “For his transformative leadership of a critical American technology company, which led to its rejuvenation for a new era of cloud computing, and for his construction of the hyperscale infrastructure that enabled the training and global deployment of American super intelligence.”

 “Each of these medalists has transformed their field or industry, laying the foundations for technologies we already can barely imagine living without,” said Michael Kratsios, Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. “While we in government work to deliver the efforts a New Golden Age of Science will require, we know that scientific progress and technological innovation depend on the insight and character of individuals. Innovators like these six awardees are the architects of the future.”

About the Science: A New Golden Age Summit:

Science: A New Golden Age, released in July 2026 by White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, is the first comprehensive rethinking of the U.S. science and technology enterprise since Vannevar Bush’s 1945 Science: The Endless Frontier.

The report observes significant changes to how scientific discovery happens today, particularly the increased role of industry in driving R&D and the close integration of applied and foundational research. It provides concrete recommendations for how government, industry, academia, and philanthropy can seize the opportunities presented by these changes to accelerate scientific discovery and empower the Nation’s best and brightest scientists. Core recommendations include strengthening support for early-career scientists, reviving the national pursuit of ambitious scientific missions, launching new funding and organizational models for transformative research, building the metascience infrastructure to continuously improve the research enterprise, and scaling SI-driven scientific discovery through the Genesis Mission.

The Science: A New Golden Age Summit convenes leading scientists and innovators to examine these changes and translate the report’s ideas into the next chapter of American scientific progress. Throughout the day, the Trump Administration will provide major announcements, in coordination with private sector partners and research institutions, to realize the vision of Science: A New Golden Age and the Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science.

Trump Accounts—tax-advantaged investment accounts for kids—are a game-changing tool designed to help every American child build savings and a stronger financial future.

With automatic enrollment now complete, the Trump Administration has made it easier than ever for families to participate and give their children a jump-start on the American Dream. Nearly 70 million Trump Accounts have now been created, including more than 60 million through automatic enrollment, giving every American child under 18, with a Social Security number, an account in their name. Now, parents or guardians just have to claim their child’s Trump Account on the Trump Accounts App and unlock what’s waiting for their child.

Today, President Donald J. Trump celebrated this historic milestone alongside Trump Account recipients, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, IRS CEO Frank Bisignano, philanthropists Michael and Susan Dell, and Brad Gerstner, whose historic contributions have helped fund millions of Trump Accounts. 

“Today we celebrate our next historic, and that’s really what it is, step to ensure every American child has a fair shot at the American dream. Today I’m pleased to announce that every single eligible minor child in America has now been automatically enrolled in a Trump account. So last summer I signed the great Big, Beautiful Bill delivering the largest tax cuts in American history, and that included in there, approved by Republicans… the Trump accounts. And under this program, the U.S. government is automatically creating a tax-free investment account for every child to grow over the course of their lives and to be used to their benefit and for their benefit after they turn 18.” – President Donald J. Trump

Trump Accounts By The Numbers:

  • Nearly 70 million Trump Accounts have been created, with more than 60 million through automatic enrollment. The Trump Administration’s automatic enrollment has created millions of Trump Accounts, making it easier than ever for families to help secure their children’s financial futures. Every American child under 18 with a valid Social Security number now has a Trump Account in their name.
  • Parents and guardians simply need to claim their child’s account through the Trump Accounts App. Claiming an account allows parents to manage it, unlock contributions from family and friends, and receive the one-time $1,000 seed contribution from for eligible children.
  • Trump Accounts are already investing billions of dollars for American children. Since their launch on July 4th, more than $4.5 billion has been deposited into Trump Accounts, including $1.3 billion in $1,000 seed contributions, over $600 million in direct contributions from family and friends, and $2.6 billion in philanthropic gifts—with more on the way.
  • Trump Accounts are reaching hardworking families across the country. An estimated 80% of accounts are linked to families earning less than $200,000 annually, putting the opportunity to build long-term savings and wealth within reach for millions of Americans.
  • Families, employers, and philanthropists can all help children build their accounts. Family and friends can contribute up to $5,000 per year; employers can contribute up to $2,500 per year, subject to the overall $5,000 annual contribution limit, and children can qualify for philanthropic contributions that are automatically deposited into their accounts. To date, more than 70 companies have already committed to Trump Account contributions for their employees.
  • Trump Accounts give children a financial foundation that can grow with them. Over time, children can watch their balance grow from a couple of thousand dollars in kindergarten to an estimated half a million dollars by retirement—while learning essential financial skills like saving, investing, compound growth, and diversification.

Trump Accounts are made possible by President Trump and Republicans’ historic Working Families Tax Cuts legislation. These tax-advantaged investment accounts— that every single Democrat voted against— are giving millions of kids a head start on building wealth and a financial stake in their future.

Today, President Donald J. Trump returns to Texas with a record of results: historic tax relief, the most secure border in a generation, safer streets, and a surge of new private investment creating jobs across the Lone Star State.

Tax Relief for Texas Workers, Families, Seniors

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts is putting money back in Texans’ pockets.

  • No Tax on Overtime: Approximately one in four Texas workers no longer pay federal income taxes on qualifying overtime pay.
  • No Tax on Social Security: About four million Texas seniors benefit from the new senior deduction.
  • Bigger Refunds: Texas taxpayers saw average refunds of $4,344 — the second-highest in the nation.
  • Rural Health Investments: Texas secured about $281 million in first-year Rural Health Transformation Program funding.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 547,000 Texas jobs, $107 billion in state GDP, and $51 billion in workers’ wages.

Safer Streets Across Texas

Violent crime is falling across the state as a result of President Trump’s law-and-order agenda.

  • Violent crime fell 13% last year, including a 13% drop in murder and 11% drop in rape.
  • The top 25 most populous jurisdictions in Texas all posted lower overall crime rates than the year before.
  • In the first half of 2026, Arlington homicides fell 60% from the first half of 2025.
  • America’s Safest Big Cities recently placed Plano, Laredo, and Arlington in the national Top 20 — with Plano and Laredo in the Top 10.

The Most Secure Border in a Generation

President Trump ended the Biden-era border crisis and is reimbursing Texas for the costs it carried.

  • The Trump Administration has not released a single illegal alien at the border for 16 straight months.
  • Southern border apprehensions in August were 94% lower than the monthly average under Biden.
  • Refugee admissions in the first ten months of this fiscal year are down almost 90% from 2024.
  • The Working Families Tax Cuts allocated $46.5 billion to finish the border wall.
  • Texas will soon receive $7.5 billion from the State Border Security Reinforcement Fund — established in the Working Families Tax Cuts — to recover costs from Biden’s border crisis.

Protecting Texas Communities

President Trump is delivering for Texas farmers, ranchers, and everyday families.

  • Water for the Valley: In January 2026, USDA and the State Department secured Mexico’s commitment to deliver 350,000 acre-feet per year from the Rio Grande — meeting the 1944 treaty average and repaying prior-cycle debt.
  • Protecting Ratepayers: After President Trump’s landmark Ratepayer Protection Pledge, the Public Utility Commission of Texas and ERCOT have moved to shield Texas families from the cost of data center expansion.
  • Screwworm Response: The Trump Administration funded additional Texas Animal Health Commission inspectors and a new $750 million sterile-fly facility, which broke ground in April at Moore Air Base in Edinburg.
  • Support for Farmers: The Trump Administration has delivered $827 million to more than 33,000 Texas farmers through the Emergency Commodity Assistance Program for the 2024 crop year. Nearly 27,000 Texas producers have also received more than $832 million in Farmer Bridge Assistance payments as part of a $12 billion national bridge program for trade disruptions and higher input costs left by the Biden Administration.

A Private Investment Boom in Texas

President Trump’s agenda of tax cuts, energy dominance, secure borders, and pro-growth policies has drawn major capital to the Lone Star State.

  • Bristol Myers Squibb announced a $2.3 billion investment to build a new multi-modal manufacturing campus in Houston.
  • Toyo Co. announced a $357 million investment to build a solar cell manufacturing facility near Houston, creating 400 American jobs.
  • Toyota announced a $3.6 billion investment at its San Antonio campus to build the new Tacoma in the United States instead of Mexico, creating 2,000 American jobs.
  • Saronic announced it will build a new $3.2 billion shipyard in Brownsville.
  • Micron announced $500 million in strategic financing to advance development and manufacturing at its Sherman facility.
  • FormFactor announced a $140 million investment for a new probe card manufacturing facility in Farmers Branch, creating more than 600 American jobs.
  • In July, ZERLUMA broke ground on a $50 million aluminum recycling and advanced manufacturing facility in Mission.
  • SpaceX announced a $16.8 billion investment for the first phase of its new semiconductor fabrication plant in Grimes County.
  • USG Corporation announced a $1.18 billion investment to build a new production facility in Orange, creating 200 American jobs.
  • Grupo Bimbo announced a $1 billion investment affirming its commitment to the U.S. market.
  • XPEL announced a $60 million investment to expand manufacturing and operations in San Antonio.
  • Tesla announced a $3 billion investment in a research chip facility at its Giga Texas campus.
  • Avant Technology announced a $20 million investment to expand its manufacturing facility in Pharr, creating 250 American jobs.
  • America First Refining and Reliance announced a multi-billion-dollar energy partnership to open the first new U.S. oil refinery in nearly half a century in Brownsville.
  • MP Materials announced a more than $1.25 billion investment in a new large-scale rare-earth magnet manufacturing campus in Northlake, creating more than 1,500 direct manufacturing and engineering jobs.
  • Arm Inc. announced a $71 million investment to expand its Austin campus with a new semiconductor lab, creating more than 320 American jobs.
  • Vantage Data Centers announced a $25 billion investment to build a 1,200-acre data center campus in Shackelford County.
  • Inventec announced an $85 million investment to build a manufacturing base in Texas to support AI server shipments.
  • Wistron announced a $500 million investment to acquire land and facilities in Dallas for high-performance computing devices.
  • LGM Pharma announced a $6 million investment to expand its Rosenberg manufacturing facility.
  • Paris Baguette announced a $160 million investment to build the company’s first North American production site, creating 450 American jobs.

President Trump and Republicans are proving once again that America First means Texas First — lower taxes, a sealed border, safer communities, and jobs that stay in the United States. Texans have a choice: continue that progress, or let Democrats tear it all down.

Last night, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order that immediately cuts diesel costs by authorizing highway use of tax-free dyed diesel and deferring the federal diesel excise tax through the end of the year. The decisive action — expected to save drivers as much as $100 per fill — puts real money back in the pockets of farmers, ranchers, truckers, loggers, and working families at the exact moment harvest demands it most.

Here’s what they’re saying:

President Donald J. Trump: “Today, I am announcing another unprecedented step to bring down costs. For many years, farm vehicles, construction equipment, and other off-road vehicles have used what is known as ‘red dye’ diesel… which is exactly the same as normal diesel, but is sold tax-free for off-road vehicles and big trucks… Tonight, I am going to sign a historic Executive Order to officially waive the off-road requirement and allow anyone to purchase tax-free red dye diesel for any reason.”

Vice President JD Vance: “Another example of President Trump acting quickly to tackle an urgent issue. In this administration, we’re fighting every day to help hard working Americans, especially our farmers.”

White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles: “President Trump signed an Executive Order right here in Nebraska to lower diesel costs for American farmers, truckers, and workers. By expanding access to red-dyed diesel and providing federal tax relief, President Trump is once again taking decisive action to put money back in the pockets of hardworking Americans. Promises made. Promises kept.”

Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins: “President Trump is the most pro ranching and farming president in our lifetime. Energy dominance is at the core of putting farmers and ranchers first. This administration has unleashed American energy dominance, and we are now the largest energy producer in the world as a result. While the Administration has structurally changed the energy sector to secure the long-term future of agriculture, we are now taking steps to deal with short term pressures impacting our American farmers. Thank you, President Trump for signing today’s Executive Order enacting enforcement discretion on on-road use of dyed diesel, which will better enable our farmers to deliver America’s harvest during this critical time. And I want to thank Vice President Vance for his help shepherding it to the end.”

American Farm Bureau Federation President Zippy Duvall: “We thank President Trump for recognizing that what happens at the fuel pump directly affects what happens on the farm and therefore at dinner tables across America. Allowing dyed diesel fuel to be used over-the-road will bring welcome relief for farmers because every cent per gallon matters when you’re running a fleet of grain trucks or hauling cattle hundreds of miles. As we detailed in a letter to the president last week, this effort will bring much needed price relief for farmers as they work to complete harvest across the U.S. The federal highway diesel tax is currently more than 24-cents per gallon, so it’s a big deal to farmers to be able to use tax exempt diesel more broadly to get their harvest to market. We appreciate that the president listened to farmers and responded.”

American Soybean Association Vice President Dave Walton: “As U.S. soybean farmers move the 2026 harvest to market, ASA thanks President Trump for his Executive Order that seeks to address high fuel costs impacting our bottom lines. This policy will align with actions taken by many soybean-producing states already, and ASA is encouraged by the administration’s continued focus on agricultural affordability.”

Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe: “Last week, I signed an executive order taking targeted action to help address the unique fuel and transportation needs of harvest season in Missouri. President Trump’s action yesterday provides commonsense flexibility to lower transportation costs and keep agriculture moving across the entire nation. When we can reduce unnecessary costs for our farmers, that ultimately benefits families across our state and nation.”

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry: “Thank you, President @realDonaldTrump! I declared a State of Emergency so our farmers could use the dyed diesel fuel they already had on hand—and now, thanks to YOU, that relief is going nationwide! This is a HUGE WIN for America’s farmers, truckers, and hardworking families. Lower costs and real relief for the people who keep this country moving.”

Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee: “On Friday, I directed TN state departments to suspend enforcement of dyed diesel restrictions through the end of October to provide relief for farmers & foresters during harvest season. Thank you, @RealDonaldTrump, for standing with the Tennesseans who feed & fuel our country.”

Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen: “This action expands on state efforts I enacted by executive order just a few weeks ago. This will greatly assist farmers who are dealing with extraordinarily high diesel prices, impacting everything they do – from field operations to transportation of their products and livestock. I appreciate that President Trump signed his order today in Nebraska. Agriculture is the tip of the spear in our great state, and we need to continue to do all that we can to feed the world and save the planet. President Trump knows that and we appreciate his support.”

Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves: “President Trump has announced he is signing an executive order that will defer the federal excise tax on dyed diesel and allow for highway use. Because of the EO signed by @POTUS, I have spoken with Commissioner @TindellSean and he plans to direct the Commercial Transportation Enforcement Division of the Mississippi Department of Public Safety to not enforce the dyed diesel prohibition on highways. Thanks to this executive order and Commissioner Tindell’s swift action, much-needed relief will be delivered to our nation’s farmers, truckers, ranchers and loggers, as well as a wide range of other industries that rely on diesel. This will have positive ripple effects on America’s economy and your wallet. I’d like to thank President Trump and his administration for working quickly to provide this relief.”

Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds: “Today, in line with President Trump’s executive order, I suspended state penalties for using dyed diesel to transport certain ag products on public roads. This will lower costs for farmers through the harvest and beyond by opening access to tax-free fuel.”

South Dakota Gov. Larry Rhoden: “In response to these extraordinary times, President Trump has ordered a suspension of enforcement of the federal dyed diesel fuel for taxpayers on highways and public roads. Therefore, I am directing the Department of Public Safety to adjust enforcement priorities regarding the use of dyed diesel fuel. Many farmers maintain on-site supplies of dyed diesel fuel for nontaxable, off-road use. By taking this action, we will provide meaningful relief to South Dakota farmers. Similarly, President Trump’s order will allow all taxpayers to realize meaningful savings from using dyed diesel.”

North Carolina Gov. Josh Stein: “Last week I took action to help provide some relief at the pump for North Carolina’s farmers, and I asked the IRS to step in to pause enforcement of the red-dyed diesel tax at the federal level. I am pleased to see farmers across the country will now get this same relief. Let’s keep working at every level of government to help people keep more money in their wallets.”

Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture Andy Holt: “Governor Lee’s directive, coupled with President Trump’s federal executive order, provides timely relief for Tennessee farmers, forest product producers and timber harvesters facing high diesel costs during harvest season. Agriculture and forestry are essential to Tennessee’s economy, and this temporary flexibility will help keep producers working, products moving, and rural communities supported. We appreciate Governor Lee’s leadership, President Trump’s action, and Secretary Rollins’ support for American agriculture.”

Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture Jonathan Shell: “Huge win for Kentucky farmers. President Trump signed an executive order expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel. With harvest underway and high fuel costs weighing on farm families, this will provide immediate relief and help lower costs. Thank you President Trump for standing with our farmers.”

Mississippi Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce Andy Gipson: “A HUGE thank you to President Trump and Governor Reeves for taking action to allow red-dyed off-road diesel fuel. A huge help to our farmers, loggers and truckers here in Mississippi and across America.”

Alabama Farmers Federation President Jimmy Parnell: “We appreciate President Trump joining Gov. Kay Ivey in allowing dyed diesel fuel to be used without penalty for highway use. With about a dozen states easing enforcement of off-road diesel rules, President Trump’s executive order provides consistency across the country and ensures farmers and timber producers will not be penalized when they cross state lines to market their products.”

Louisiana Farm Bureau President Richard Fontenot: “Anything helps, especially as we work to get the crops out of the fields. I’m appreciative of the governor’s (and president’s) efforts to give us any relief during this time.”

Tennessee Farm Bureau Federation: “We join American Farm Bureau President @ZippyDuvall in applauding the executive order signed by President Trump to suspend enforcement of dyed diesel fuel restrictions for agricultural operators, giving farmers a break.”

Sen. Tom Cotton: “Allowing on-road use of red diesel will give Arkansas farmers much-needed relief. This is a welcome step by the administration that I’ve long called for.”

Sen. Chuck Grassley: “Thx to Pres Trump for listening to farmers & temporarily allowing off-road dyed diesel for highway use Lowering costs for FARMERS DURING HARVEST”

Sen. Bill Hagerty: “@POTUS is taking action to lower diesel prices, cutting costs for Tennessee farmers who keep food moving from the farm to families’ dinner tables.”

Sen. Roger Marshall: “Temporary expanded use of dyed diesel allows producers to utilize more fuel options during harvest and lightens the cost of production for farmers and ranchers at a crucial time. Thanks to the White House for listening to farmers. We still have more work to do.”

Sen. Mike Rounds: “Following my letter last week, I’m pleased to see that the President is taking steps to lower fuel prices, including a review of certain taxes on diesel. This is an opportunity to offer real relief to South Dakotans who continue to pay higher prices at the pump, particularly farmers and ranchers who are in the middle of harvest. We’ll continue to work on addressing the high cost of living impacting our state.”

Rep. Mark Alford: “@POTUS just signed an order letting truckers and farmers run tax-free dyed diesel on the highway through year’s end — no interest, no penalties. That puts real money back in the pockets of the folks who haul our freight and grow our food.”

Rep. Tim Burchett: “A few weeks ago, I called on @POTUS to take action on diesel prices. Last night, President Trump signed an Executive Order to put money back in the pockets of American farmers, truckers, and workers.”

Rep. Don Davis: “It’s a much needed Executive Order that provides temporary relief for farmers and working families facing record fuel costs.”

Rep. Russell Fry: “No one cares more about affordability than President Trump and Congressional Republicans.”

Rep. Ashley Hinson: “High diesel prices are hurting our truckers, farmers, and all Iowans, and this executive order is a step in the right direction to deliver relief. We should be using every tool available to lower fuel prices and provide flexibility for Iowa farmers during harvest season. I’ll continue to push for bipartisan policies that lower costs at the pump and the checkout line.”

Rep. Rich McCormick: “A farmer can’t wait for prices to come down. The crop is in the field right now. This week @POTUS signed an order that temporarily allows tax-free dyed diesel to be used on the highway. The federal diesel tax is deferred through the end of the year, with no interest and no penalties. That’s about $60 on a 250-gallon fill, and more where states follow suit. It’s temporary, and it’s not the whole answer. But for the families who feed America, it is real relief at a critical time. The long-term fix is more supply and more refining capacity. That is the work still ahead.”

Rep. Zach Nunn: “This is a good first step and it will deliver real relief for farmers facing record diesel prices in the middle of harvest.”

Rep. Jason Smith: “I applaud President Trump’s executive order today to provide immediate relief by deferring the excise tax for on-road use of dyed diesel until the end of the year. This is a much-needed step to lessen the burden that increased fuel prices have had on farmers, ranchers, and the entire agricultural community. This executive order is only a first step — it is crucial to provide lasting relief for the hardworking Americans who feed, fuel, and clothe our nation.”

Rep. Greg Steube: “President Trump is delivering relief for America’s farmers and truckers. My RED Fuel Act is sitting in Congress waiting to make this relief permanent. House Leadership needs to bring us back to D.C. and pass it!”

The post WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: President Trump Delivers Immediate Diesel Relief, Saving Americans Up to $100 Per Fill appeared first on The White House.

Today, President Donald J. Trump travels to Grand Island, Nebraska. Under President Trump and Republican leadership, families in the Cornhusker State are keeping more of what they earn, farmers and ranchers are getting direct support, private investment is expanding production, and crime is falling in the state’s largest cities.

Historic Tax Relief for Nebraskans

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts stopped the largest tax hike in American history and put money back in Nebraskans’ pockets.

  • No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime: Qualified tips and overtime pay are now deductible from federal income taxes, benefiting hundreds of thousands of Nebraska service workers, truckers, manufacturers, and hourly employees.
  • No Tax on Social Security: More than 300,000 Nebraska seniors can benefit from the new deduction that eliminates federal income tax on Social Security benefits for the vast majority of recipients.
  • Bigger refunds: Nebraskans’ average federal tax refund reached $3,378.
  • Investments in rural health: Nebraska secured nearly $219 million in first-year funding under the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program — the eighth-largest award in the country — to modernize care in rural communities.
  • Protecting Nebraska’s economy: The Working Families Tax Cuts protected 37,000 Nebraska jobs, preserved $7 billion in state GDP, and safeguarded $3 billion in wages for Nebraskans.

Standing with Nebraska Farmers and Ranchers

President Trump’s America First agenda is delivering real dollars and new market access to the producers who feed the country.

  • Year-round E15: In April 2025, President Trump’s EPA granted the emergency waiver that cleared summer sales of E15 nationwide, answering the direct request of Nebraska and other Midwestern states and expanding the market for Nebraska ethanol and corn.
  • Direct aid: USDA has delivered $622 million to 36,000 Nebraska Farmers through the Emergency Commodity Assistance Program for the 2024 crop year. Nebraska farmers have also received more than $632 million in Farmer Bridge Assistance payments — part of the $12 billion national bridge program for trade disruptions and higher input costs left by the Biden Administration — with nearly 33,000 Nebraska producers applying. They remain eligible for the $16 billion Supplemental Disaster Relief Program covering 2023 and 2024 crop losses.
  • Ranchers first: In September 2026, President Trump signed two Executive Orders backing American ranchers. One directs action to help producers protect herds from wolves and other predators, and advances country-of-origin labeling transparency. The second orders tougher enforcement of the Packers and Stockyards Act and expands ranchers’ ability to get cattle to market without compromising food safety.

New Investment Across Nebraska

President Trump’s economic agenda is delivering major private-sector investment and expansion.

  • Eaton is investing more than $30 million in a new Bellevue facility to expand U.S. production of medium-voltage switchgear for data centers, creating more than 200 new jobs.
  • Becton Dickinson is investing $110 million to expand prefillable syringe production at its Columbus plant, creating about 120 new jobs, on top of its earlier $35 million investment at the same plant.

Safer Communities for Nebraskans

President Trump’s commitment to law and order is producing real drops in crime in Nebraska’s largest cities.

  • In Omaha, crime is down from last year, including an 11% drop in total crime, a 12% drop in property crime, a 33% drop in criminal homicide, a 21% drop in rape, a 31% drop in robbery, and a 29% drop in auto theft.
  • In Lincoln, violent crime is down 15%, robbery is down 31%, aggravated assault is down 16%, murder is down 75%, and property crime is down 9%.

President Trump is in Nebraska to deliver a simple message: promises made, promises kept. Lower taxes, stronger farms and ranches, new manufacturing, and safer streets are the record because Republicans delivered — and Nebraskans cannot afford to hand that progress back.

KYOTO, JAPAN — At the 23rd Annual Meeting of the Science and Technology in Society (STS) Forum convened in Kyoto, the United States and 16 countries endorsed the Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science. The joint declaration reflects a shared ambition  to renew and strengthen our science ecosystems and usher in a golden age of discovery and prosperity.

Led by White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, the Kyoto Vision recognizes that we stand at the frontier of an immense opportunity to harness super intelligence and advance new approaches to greatly accelerate scientific discovery. Super intelligence for science will enable autonomous experimentation at scale, unlocking new experimental and analytical capabilities that open entirely new lines of inquiry. In light of the profound shifts in the research landscape, ministers pledged to seize this moment by harnessing new institutional models and funding mechanisms to enable the best and brightest scientists to pursue their most ambitious work. 

“The way we make scientific discoveries has changed, and the Kyoto Vision is a recognition of that shift and a call to action,” said Director Kratsios. “Super intelligence applied to science will be the greatest force in history for democratizing research. Seizing this moment requires us to reinvigorate our research enterprises and leverage new institutional models for discovery. Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States is leading that charge, and the Kyoto Vision shows the world is ready to move forward with us.”

The Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science calls for:

  • Improving the institutions of discovery: Ministers noted the value of a using a variety of funding tools to support research, including long-duration awards, rapid grants, and prizes and challenges, and encouraged experimentation with new institutional models that offer different levels of autonomy, resources, and direction. They welcomed metascience as an empirical field to improve how science is conducted, organized, and funded for public benefit.
  • Harnessing super intelligence for science: Ministers recognized that SI is both accelerating existing research tasks and enabling entirely new forms of inquiry. They encouraged thoughtful integration of SI into scientific workflows and pledged to expand researcher access to SI for science tools, scientific data, computing infrastructure, and experimental facilities.
  • Cultivating talent across the scientific enterprise: Ministers committed to identifying and investing in meritorious students and early-career researchers, and to giving them the support, freedom, and opportunity necessary for ambitious inquiry. They acknowledged that progress in many technological domains depends on people who can operate, maintain, and improve instrumentation, and encouraged expanded hands-on training as well as cross-sectoral doctoral programs, fellowships, and research partnerships.

In July 2026, Director Kratsios delivered to President Trump Science: A New Golden Age, the most comprehensive rethinking of the American science and technology research enterprise in eight decades. The report established new directions for U.S. government agencies on how they conduct, fund, and measure the impact of R&D, in light of fundamental changes to the American scientific enterprise and the new opportunities that have emerged.

Iowa Speaker of the House Pat Grassley: “This project would be a gamechanger for southeast Iowa and leave a lasting impact on our state’s manufacturing footprint. This will bring real jobs that mean stable careers for working families, giving more young people a chance to proudly call Iowa home. I’ve made it my mission in the Iowa House to make sure we bring opportunities for growth to all parts of the state and delivering this plant follows through on that promise.”

Iowa Senate Majority Leader Mike Klimesh: “For years, we have been passing legislation to help Iowa grow, draw people to our rural communities, and strengthen our state’s economy. Iowa State Rep. Carter Nordman: “$15 BILLION dollar investment in Iowa (largest ever, by far)! Thank you President Donald J. Trump & Governor Kim Reynolds for your leadership on this historic project!”

Today, President Donald J. Trump announced one of the largest steel plants in American history: a $15 billion Mesabi Metallics mill in Iowa. The project will create 1,750 permanent Iowa jobs, support up to 6,000 construction jobs, and is projected to add $95 billion to the U.S. economy over the next decade.

The mill will produce 7.5 million tons of steel per year in its first phase, rising to about ten million tons, using iron ore from Mesabi Metallics’ newly opened Minnesota mine — the first new iron ore mine in the United States in 50 years.

This is the kind of project Democrats spent years making impossible. The Obama Administration blocked a proposed northern Minnesota copper-nickel mine by denying its federal lease renewals in 2016. The Biden Administration canceled those same leases in 2022, then banned mining for 20 years across 225,504 acres of the Superior National Forest. It revoked a key federal water permit for another long-stalled copper-nickel mine. It blocked a 211-mile road in Alaska that would’ve opened a major copper and cobalt district. In 2024, it piled new rules onto taconite iron-ore processing and coke ovens — the plants that feed American steel — while tariff loopholes kept foreign steel flowing in.

President Trump reversed those policies — and American mining is roaring ahead.

  • In 2025, the U.S. surpassed Japan in crude steel production for the first time since 1999 and became the world’s third-largest steel producer. In fact, raw steel output is up 9% since President Trump returned to office.
  • Nearly 6,000 steelworker jobs have been added after almost 10,000 were lost under the prior Administration.
  • American mills now supply 84% of the U.S. finished steel market, up from 77% in 2024.
  • Steel imports are falling as tariffs, permitting reforms, and energy dominance bring production home.
  • New mill orders hit a record $17.3 billion in July 2026; domestic shipments hit a record $16.9 billion that same month.
  • U.S. manufacturing has expanded for eight straight months.

Today, President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump concluded a historic state visit with His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of the People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan. This marked the first visit to the White House by a Chinese President in more than a decade — and the first time a Chinese leader has made two formal state visits to the United States.

As President Trump said, “The meeting was one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the U.S.A… Much has been, and will be, accomplished.”

  • President Trump and the First Lady welcomed President Xi and Madame Peng with an official state arrival ceremony: “President Xi, Madame Peng, and the members of the Chinese delegation, I am delighted to welcome you to the beautiful White House.”
  • President Trump and the First Lady hosted a full official state welcome, including a gift exchange, Silent Drill Platoon review, military review, and flyover — a commanding display of American strength and hospitality.
  • President Trump and President Xi held productive bilateral discussions: “I think our farmers are going to be very happy — a lot of very positive things happened… Great things for both countries. It’s just been very, very productive.”
  • President Trump presented President Xi and Madame Peng with a custom-made statue of a bald eagle at the state dinner: “The bald eagle is a national symbol of the United States and an embodiment of the free and soaring spirit of America — and we hope it will find a nice place, a wonderful place, in Beijing.”
  • President Trump toasted President Xi and Madame Peng at the state dinner: “May all of our people know a future of harmony, peace, and success.”
  • President Trump gave President Xi an exclusive tour of Marine One and the new South Lawn helipad: “He likes granite. He’s an expert on stone, aside from many other things, and he loves good granite.”
  • President Trump and the First Lady hosted tea for President Xi and Madame Peng: “We’ve had a tremendous visit from two spectacular people, and we really enjoyed it — and I think we’ve made tremendous strides. We’ve made great strides. Very positive for both countries.”
  • President Trump and the First Lady hosted President Xi and Madame Peng at the National Archives in recognition of the 250th anniversary of American independence.

This state visit showcased the strength of the United States, advanced American economic interests, and made one thing unmistakable: peace and prosperity are strongest when America leads from a position of power.

The attacks on President Donald J. Trump’s public service announcements are highly dishonest. The announcements are very clearly not campaign ads; President Trump is not on the ballot and there is no call to action. Instead, the announcements are a reminder for Americans to love their country and know why it’s worth defending — at home, at the border, and abroad.

That’s not partisanship — that’s a government that still believes in the country it serves.

Administrations of both parties have used public service announcements to explain policy and make the case for the nation’s direction:

  • The G.W. Bush Administration ran a national television campaign explaining the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act to seniors. It also bought Super Bowl airtime for anti-drug and anti-terrorism public service announcements.
  • The Obama Administration used national advertising to promote Obamacare subsidies and open enrollment, and a digital campaign to sell its Waters of the United States rule.
  • The Biden Administration poured hundreds of millions of dollars into “We Can Do This” — television, digital, radio, and print spots — to drive a nationwide public health message.
  • It’s not just modern Administrations. President Woodrow Wilson’s Committee on Public Information used posters, films, and speakers to rally the country. President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s Office of War Information produced films, radio, and posters to promote the war effort.

When prior Administrations utilized the airwaves, it was called “public education.” When this Administration promotes pride in our country, many of those same voices call it “propaganda.”

Patriotism isn’t partisan. These public service announcements are unapologetically American, clearly disclosed, and aimed at the country — not a line on the ballot.

President Donald J. Trump is ensuring America is respected on the world stage again and holding the U.N. accountable after years of weak and failed Democrat leadership under the Biden Administration that put America last.

Under President Donald J. Trump’s leadership, America is back and stronger than ever before.

President Donald J.   • President Trump secured an agreement with Denmark and Greenland that permanently guarantees U.S. security interests in the Arctic at zero cost to the American taxpayer.

  • U.S. forces captured the Venezuelan dictator and indicted narcoterrorist Nicolás Maduro and his wife. Since then, the Trump Administration has worked closely with Venezuela’s leadership for a brighter future for the people of Venezuela and America. 
  • President Trump has secured the biggest oil deal in world history for the American people, delivering the U.S. majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela.
  • The Trump Administration is rooting out the Cuban regime’s coordination with radical and communist networks in the U.S. that sow division and threaten the American way of life, and taking action against the Mexican cartels that pursue terror against Americans. 
  • President Trump successfully pressured Panama to withdraw from China’s Belt and Road Initiative.
  • President Trump ended eight wars, ensured the release of all remaining hostages in Gaza, and is paving the way for lasting stability in the Middle East.
  • President Trump raised NATO member defense spending to 5% of GDP and secured billions in investments from NATO partners into the U.S. defense industry, creating thousands of new jobs, protecting hundreds of thousands of American jobs, and boosting allied security. 
  • President Trump designated Muslim Brotherhood branches as Foreign Terrorist Organizations and redesignated the Houthis as a Foreign Terrorist Organization to ensure the U.S. can eliminate their capabilities, operations, and threats posed to Americans and our national security. 
  • President Trump is rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, restoring American shipbuilding, and reshoring critical industries. These policies are reshoring American manufacturing, creating new high-paying jobs, and securing over $11 trillion in investments across the United States.


President Trump will never stop fighting for the American people, and he’s only just begun.
