Today, President Donald J. Trump joined leaders of Denmark and Greenland to sign an unprecedented agreement giving the United States lasting control over security interests in Greenland. The landmark agreement — which comes at no cost to American taxpayers — forever guarantees America the ability to defend the continent, includes permanent basing rights, and bars any U.S. adversary from establishing a base, military presence, or sensitive investment without America’s approval.

The agreement is being hailed at home and around the world as a decisive victory for American security and a stronger NATO in the Arctic. Here’s what they’re saying:

President Donald J. Trump: “As I announced just days ago, the U.S. has also reached an unprecedented agreement regarding the Northern Frontier of North America — the large and strategically vital piece of land known as Greenland. This agreement… gives the United States permanent control over security and all other needs on that territory. We will have the complete ability to do what is necessary to defend the American continent.”

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen: “This day represents a milestone in our longstanding cooperation. 75 years ago, we entered into an agreement about the defense of Greenland. Today, we are signing an even bigger and better agreement — a deal that can last forever. This deal is good for the United States, it’s good for Greenland, for Denmark, for the NATO alliance, and therefore, also good for Europe. In other words, we are strengthening our common security, boosting our common deterrence, showing our adversaries who we are — and we are doing it together.”

Prime Minister of Greenland Jens-Frederik Nielsen: “We are, have been, and will remain a steadfast friend of the United States and a part of the Western alliance. Your security is our security and our security is your security. We are truly pleased with the result that strengthens our shared security and strengthens our bond as close allies. This agreement is historical.”

Danish Minister for Foreign Affairs Lars Løkke Rasmussen: “An important moment today. Greenland, Denmark and the United States have signed an agreement strengthening security in the Arctic and North Atlantic. It’s been a bumpy ride. But here we are – with a deal in hand that we can all be very satisfied with. We share a long history. And we share a responsibility for the security of our region. Today, we take another important step together – with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark and the Greenlandic people’s right to self-determination. History binds us together. Our future demands that we stand together.”

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte: “Great to see the deal signed by the United States, Denmark, and Greenland today. We know the threats we face, and greater security in the Arctic and North Atlantic is essential for Europe and North America alike. This agreement, along with NATO’s growing role in securing this vital region, enhances our collective security and supports a safer and more stable future for us all”

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen: “I welcome today’s agreement on strengthening security in the Arctic and North Atlantic. My visit to Greenland earlier this month underscored the strategic importance of the region and the scale of the challenges. Challenges we will face together. As always, the EU will work closely with Denmark and Greenland and our international partners.”

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz: “Good news for the security of Greenland: The agreement between Denmark, Greenland, and the USA strengthens our partnership in NATO and security in the High North. Our partners can count on the support of Germany.”

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre: “I welcome the agreement between Greenland, Denmark and the USA. It is a good diplomatic solution, important for stability and security in the [Arctic].”

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni: “Well done on the agreement between the United States, Denmark, and Greenland. The Arctic is a strategic area: security is built together.”

Estonian Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna: “Estonia welcomes the agreement reached by Denmark, Greenland and the United States to strengthen security in the Arctic. Enhanced cooperation among NATO Allies in Greenland and the Arctic reinforces the security of the Alliance and of Europe as a whole. Close and coordinated cooperation among Allies remains the most effective way to strengthen deterrence and defence in the region.”

Swedish Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard: “I welcome that Denmark, Greenland and the United States have reached an agreement on strengthened security in the Arctic and North-Atlantic area. Sweden remains committed to working with all our Allies to improve our common security.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio: “This historic deal is a huge win for the United States and the American people. Thanks to President Trump’s vision and leadership, this historic agreement permanently guarantees U.S. security interests in the Arctic at zero cost to the U.S. taxpayer. Greenland will forever be part of the strategic defense area of North America and exclude any adversary from it and the surrounding area. This deal permanently and completely addresses our national security concerns in Greenland.”

U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz: “History in the making at UNGA as President Trump seals his landmark deal with Denmark and Greenland ensuring American national security and defense in the Arctic region.”

U.S. Ambassador to Denmark Kenneth Howery: “Historic day for the United States, Denmark, and Greenland. A tremendous honor to join President Trump, Prime Minister Frederiksen, and Prime Minister Nielsen in New York today as they sign an agreement to ensure all three of our countries’ security for generations to come.”

U.S. Special Envoy to Greenland Jeff Landry: “This is a great day for America and for our national security interests. Well done President @realDonaldTrump and @SecRubio! With the signing of this deal, American interests in the Arctic have never been more secure. This is America First. This is promises made, promises kept!”

Former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich: “In 1946, President Truman’s administration explored purchasing Greenland because of its importance to American defense. Eighty years later, President Trump has announced a new Arctic security agreement. The geography hasn’t changed. The strategic competition has.”

Former Deputy National Security Advisor KT McFarland: “Game changer”

Former National Security Council Chief of Staff Alex Gray: “Nearly two years ago I wrote in @WSJopinion that POTUS should actually buy #Greenland. He has now scored a remarkable victory that accomplishes those goals without the cost.”

Center for Security Policy Senior Fellow Col. Grant Newsham (ret.): “This is a big deal. This is right up there with Secretary of State Seward getting Alaska. It’s a little different because we haven’t bought the place, but it locks up or brings into the fold, really, key terrain, key geography, up on our northeast… Russia and the Chinese, in particular, they can’t get in there militarily, and they cannot get in economically.”

Washington Times Editorial Board: “Coming on the heels of his Venezuela triumph — access to the world’s largest known oil reserves — President Trump’s Greenland deal caps his status as one of history’s great dealmakers.”

Commentator Scott Jennings: “Donald Trump was right about Greenland from the beginning… and finally, we got it done. This historic agreement between the United States and Denmark gives Donald Trump everything we wanted and everything we needed as it relates to the future security of Greenland.”

Claremont Institute Senior Fellow Jeremy Carl: “This is a major win for which President Trump, Secretary Rubio and the administration are not getting nearly enough credit. It will dramatically fortify our Arctic security while permanently keeping out Russian and Chinese meddling. Denmark keeps its sovereignty and Greenland keeps its rights of self-determination– neither of which were core issues for America in any case. This is an actual win-win for all parties involved and it would not have happened without early and very visible U.S. pressure (highlighted by VP Vance’s visit) all of which were met by howls of criticism from the corporate media and foreign policy ‘experts.’”

Commentator Hugh Hewitt: “To repeat, this is an enormous deal.  Keep score on who downplays it or minimizes its importance. President Trump has secured part of the gateway to the Arctic —an unqualified big win. Those that won’t admit it will also have likely damned POTUS for straining relations with Denmark and NATO over elevating the topic from the start of his second term. Now that is behind the allies, the threats are identified and excluded, access guaranteed for Golden Dome facilities and any other basing needs.  Sheesh TDS is a powerful drug.”

Fox Business Network host David Asman: “For all the hullabaloo, it looks like we ended up with a good Greenland deal.”

Just the News Editor-in-Chief John Solomon: “This deal not only strengthens national security but also addresses longstanding strategic concerns in the region.”

Commentator Dan Bongino: “…a generational security deal with GREENLAND has been agreed to, the border is CLOSED, the streets are SAFER, we’re BUILDING things in America again, and Donald J. Trump is the President of the United States of America.”

Commentator David Burke: “As I learn the incredible news that Denmark has signed an agreement granting the United States military installation rights in Greenland, I can’t help smiling at the way President Trump steered this historic event. The Media & the Democrats got it all wrong AGAIN!”

NewsNation host Katie Pavlich: “Manifest Destiny continues 🇺🇸”

Commentator Glenn Beck: “If you look at the last two years, it’s clear President Trump is preparing for something big. He’s securing permanent security control over Greenland, kicked China out of the Panama Canal, and locked up 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil. For 25 years, China quietly bought up our backyard to gain a strategic stranglehold on our side of the globe. In just 20 months, Trump pulled the rug right out from under them. While the rest of the world fractures, Trump is building a completely self-sufficient Western Hemisphere. One where America controls its own destiny without bowing to Beijing or Tehran.”

Strategy Risks Vice President Melissa Chen: “This is a big deal… Your future as a North American depends on it. This deal constitutes a strategy of denial for China’s Arctic ambitions and Russia’s Arctic militarization, two revisionist powers that have been probing NATO’s northern edge and the GIUK gap, the gateway to the Atlantic: Donroe Doctrine FTW”

Columnist Gordon Chang: “President Trump is securing the Arctic with the historic Greenland deal.”

Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton: “Great news for our national security on Greenland from @realDonaldTrump!”

Commentator Mark Levin: “POTUS is unbelievable! He pulled it off!”

American Conservative Union Chairman Matt Schlapp: “Like the Wall he just kept pushing and now it’s a reality. Never seen anything like it.”

Martin Capital CEO Rod D. Martin: “With today’s signing of the tripartite deal between the United States, Greenland, and Denmark, Donald Trump has achieved yet another masterstroke — like the NATO commitment to increase defense spending more than two-and-a-half times, like the EU trade deal, like booting China out of Panama.”

Commentator Marc Thiessen: “Greenland problem solved!”

Sen. Jim Banks: “They said it couldn’t be done, but @POTUS just proved the foreign policy establishment wrong again. This historic agreement with Denmark ensures the United States and our allies will be able to secure Greenland and the High North against our adversaries for generations to come.”

Sen. Bill Hagerty: “It’s hard to overstate the monumental impact of @POTUS ‘s historic agreement with the Kingdom of Denmark and Greenland. Many thought an achievement of this magnitude was impossible, but @realDonaldTrump has proven once again that he knows the art of the deal. America is the leader of the free world, and this accomplishment will forever stand as a pivotal moment for security at home and abroad.”

Sen. Mike Lee: “We’ve got Greenland! This is what winning looks like.”

Sen. Dave McCormick: “Greenland is vital to America’s national security. @POTUS ‘s deal gives America permanent military access while Greenland remains under Danish sovereignty. This terrific development will play a pivotal role in American’s Golden Dome Defense and strengthen deterrence as China and Russia expand their presence in the Arctic.”

Sen. Lisa Murkowski: “I’m encouraged that our nations have reached a breakthrough that respects Greenlandic self-determination and the sovereignty of the Kingdom of Denmark while strengthening our shared security in the Arctic. I’m hopeful that this agreement will build upon the longstanding framework established by the 1951 Defense of Greenland Agreement, adapting our cooperation to address today’s security challenges while preserving the foundation that has supported our partnership. I have always had faith in the enduring friendship between the United States, Greenland, and Denmark, and I believe this agreement represents an important opportunity to further strengthen our bond.”

Republican Study Committee: “President Trump proved once again that it is possible to put Americans first while strengthening security for our allies and partners around the world. This historic Greenland deal is a major win for American national security.”

Rep. Brian Babin: “This is a major development and a critical step forward for our national security. Thank you, President Trump, for securing this historic agreement!”

Rep. Michael Cloud: “Today’s agreement on Greenland is significant. It gives the United States permanent control over security in the region and ensures no adversary can establish a presence without our approval. Having visited Pituffik Space Base, the strategic importance of this place is clear.”

Rep. Pat Fallon: “Excellent news for US national security.”

Rep. Randy Fine: “President Trump locked down security control of Greenland so Russia and China can never use it against us. Other presidents talked about it, he got it done. Yet another win for America delivered by President Trump.”

Rep. Lance Gooden: “The ‘experts’ insisted a deal over Greenland was impossible. President Trump has proven them wrong once more. This landmark agreement with Denmark and Greenland will help safeguard U.S. national security for generations to come!”

Rep. Nicole Malliotakis: “The security agreement signed today will strengthen the United States military and strategic position in the Arctic while preventing China and Russia from gaining footholds in the region. Greenland’s strategic location and rare-earth resources make it vital to America’s national and economic security and I applaud President Trump for negotiating this critical and consequential deal.”

Rep. Rich McCormick: “Greenland is critical to America’s national security. President Trump secured a landmark deal that defends our national interests, keeps our adversaries out, and makes America safer. Peace through strength. America First.”

Rep. John Moolenaar: “Permanently controlling Greenland’s security is a tremendous victory for President Trump and the American people. Greenland is home to critical minerals that will power the future and it can never fall under the control of China or Russia. China has often tried to stake false illegitimate claims in the Arctic and this agreement will ensure it never has a foothold in Greenland.”

Rep. Andy Ogles: “President Trump did what no other president could: He secured Greenland and with it the complete security of North America. This is OUR hemisphere. MAKE GREENLAND GREAT AGAIN!”

Today, President Donald J. Trump addressed the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly and delivered a powerful message: American strength and resolve is back.   • “Two and a half centuries after the cause of liberty found its home on this continent, I can report to you with pride that America is back, and our country is stronger today than ever before.” (Watch)
  • “As President of the most extraordinary nation in history, I have no interest in leaving dangers to grow for another day. I do not believe in letting problems fester; they only become harder to solve. So, while others have talked, I have acted. While others have spoken of peace, I have made peace. While others have ignored threats, I have confronted them. While others have talked of courage, America has shown it. While others have promised strength, I have used it to make America the most powerful country in the world. Working with many nations in this room, we are solving decades of intractable challenges — and we are settling years of unfinished business.” (Watch)

Last week, President Donald J. Trump removed CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House grounds after years of false reporting. The First Amendment protects their right to publish; it does not entitle them to a hard pass, briefing room seat, or place in the press pool.

Access changes are nothing new. What is new, however, is the sudden claim that it becomes sacred only when the outlets are friendly to the Radical Left. The rule was never “every outlet gets in.” It was always “our side stays in.”

For years, Democrat Administrations have restricted, punished, and locked out the press.

2009: The Obama White House branded Fox News as the “research arm” and “communications arm” of the Republican Party, barred it from a round of exclusive Sunday show interviews, instructed agencies to “skip” including it in pooled coverage, derided it as “really not news,” and undertook an all-out effort to isolate the organization. Barack Hussein Obama now calls a Fox ban “unimaginable,” but his White House tried it — and his spokesman admitted they were willing to do it.

2010: The Obama Justice Department labeled Fox News correspondent James Rosen a possible “co-conspirator” in a criminal leak case, secretly monitored his emails and phone calls, and tracked his movements — an “unprecedented” level of surveillance and intimidation of a journalist over his reporting.

2011: Obama White House officials restricted the Boston Herald from coverage — writing that pool slots depended on covering Obama “fairly” — after the paper ran a front page Mitt Romney op-ed.

2011: After a San Francisco Chronicle reporter recorded protesters interrupting an Obama fundraiser, White House officials threatened to strip the outlet from access and warned of retaliation if the paper reported on it.

2012: The Obama Justice Department secretly seized two months of telephone records covering more than 20 Associated Press lines used by more than a dozen journalists — targeting them over their reporting.

2023: The Biden White House blocked New York Post reporter Steven Nelson from covering the President’s only daytime public event — despite empty seats in the room — after the reporter pressed Biden on his family’s shady business dealings.

2023: The Biden Administration restricted more than 440 reporters from White House access through a new, retroactive press credentialing process — with independent and conservative journalists taking a heavy share of the hit. The White House Correspondents’ Association barely objected.

2008: In the Obama campaign’s final days, senior campaign officials pulled reporters from three prominent outlets off the traveling press plane — restricting them from coverage after the papers endorsed Obama’s opponent.

2021: The same media now suing once urged a ban on Fox News. CNN’s Brian Stelter repeatedly floated removing Fox News from the White House press tool as a “political tool,” and later even suggested Fox News be dropped from cable altogether.

During the first 100 days of President Trump’s second term, the Media Research Center found that 92% of coverage by mainstream outlets was negative compared to nearly 60% positive coverage during the same period under Biden. That’s more like a political operation with cameras than a free press holding power to account.

No President is required to host a hostile operation on the grounds. Access has always been a privilege — and President Trump is applying that rule.

On Wednesday, September 16th, 2026, G20 Energy Ministers concluded the Energy Abundance Ministerial in Houston, Texas. The Ministerial was hosted by the White House National Energy Dominance Council (NEDC), the Department of the Interior, the Department of Energy, and the Environmental Protection Agency.

At the conclusion of the Ministerial, G20 Ministers reached consensus on four outcomes advancing energy access, infrastructure development, water resilience, and supply chain security. The outcomes advance the Energy Abundance Working Group’s three pillars: Energy Security and Affordable Baseload, Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency, and Critical Minerals and Resilient Supply Chains. Together, they support the common sense solutions that President Trump has championed to increase energy availability, speed the development of critical infrastructure, strengthen water resilience, and reduce vulnerabilities in the supply chains essential to modern economies.

Ministers reached consensus on deliverables that support affordable, scalable, and context-specific pathways to expand household energy access, including the use of liquefied petroleum gas, or LPG, where it is a reliable and scalable means of rapidly displacing traditional biomass. They also reached agreement on Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency to encourage more efficient, predictable, and effective domestic permitting and regulatory processes, and a Water Reuse Initiative outlining voluntary, fit-for-purpose water reuse to strengthen resilience for communities, energy production, manufacturing, agriculture, and other critical sectors. Finally, Ministers agreed in the Critical Minerals Statement on voluntary cooperation to build resilient, affordable, secure, and diversified critical minerals value chains through information sharing, innovation, investment, capacity building, and local value addition.

“The world cannot build secure energy systems, advanced manufacturing capacity, or digital infrastructure on fragile mineral supply chains,” said Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum, Chair of the National Energy Dominance Council. “The consensus reached in Houston supports a common sense approach: diversify supply, strengthen domestic and regional capacity, encourage investment and innovation, and respect each nation’s sovereignty over its natural resources. These steps will help reduce overreliance on any single supplier while creating more durable supply chains and greater economic opportunity.”

“Energy is the essential ingredient that enables everything we do,” said Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “A highly energized society brings health, wealth, and opportunity. The consensus reached in Houston advances cooperation to expand the affordable, reliable, and secure energy, infrastructure, and supply chains needed to support prosperity, resilience, and opportunity throughout the world.”

“President Trump’s energy abundance agenda reflects reality – strong environmental stewardship and economic prosperity go hand in hand,” said Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin. “The consensus reached in Houston advances solutions that streamline processes without sacrificing safeguards, expand water resilience, and enable the infrastructure needed to deliver reliable and affordable energy. This is how the G20 can support growth, protect communities, and meet the demands of the future.”

The investments and agreements announced in Houston demonstrate how President Trump’s energy abundance agenda is creating jobs, delivering economic opportunity, strengthening American manufacturing, and expanding the energy infrastructure needed to power the future. The Japanese company Hitachi Energy announced a $528 million investment to build a new power transformer manufacturing facility in Gallman, Mississippi, expected to create 654 new jobs. Houston-based Caturus announced a five-train expansion of its Commonwealth LNG export facility in Louisiana that would add 7.75 million tonnes per annum of capacity and nearly double the project’s planned capacity to approximately 17.25 million tonnes per annum, Continental Resources signed a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela’s PDVSA to develop and operate the 126,000-acre Ayacucho 2 Block in the Orinoco Belt, which Continental estimates contains approximately 30 billion barrels of oil.

At the Ministerial, Administrator Zeldin announced the EPA’s repeal of the majority of the Biden Administration’s greenhouse gas requirements for U.S. power plants, the largest power sector deregulatory action in American history. EPA projects the repeal will save $310 billion and help unleash America’s vast energy resources, including coal and natural gas. The Administrator also proposed to repeal the remaining power sector standards, which would save an additional $370 million in direct compliance costs. Together, these actions will restore reliable, affordable baseload power and strengthen American energy dominance.

Representatives from the following nations and unions were present at the three-day Ministerial: the African Union, the Argentine Republic, the Commonwealth of Australia, the Federative Republic of Brazil, Canada, the People’s Republic of China, the European Union, the French Republic, the Federal Republic of Germany, the Republic of India, the Republic of Indonesia, the Italian Republic, Japan, the United Mexican States, the Republic of Poland, the Russian Federation, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Republic of Korea, the Republic of Türkiye, and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

For decades, Presidents have promised to cut prescription drug prices, but only President Donald J. Trump has delivered. Prescription drug prices have now recorded their sharpest annual drop in more than 60 years — and those lower prices now reach every Medicaid program in America.

President Trump is the first President to actually lower prescription drug prices.

Official data confirms the largest annual decline in more than 60 years — the steepest drop since 1963 — with prices falling every month of 2026.

President Trump ended the era of Americans paying the highest drug prices on Earth.

Through Most Favored Nation pricing, 26 of the world’s largest drugmakers — covering 90% of the branded U.S. market — have agreed to bring U.S. prices in line with the lowest paid by comparable developed nations. These agreements are projected to save Americans more than $600 billion.

Every state Medicaid program in the nation now gets Most Favored Nation drug prices.

All 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico are in, unlocking nearly $65 billion in Medicaid drug savings over the next decade — real relief for low-income families, children, seniors, and the disabled, and another big win for taxpayers.

TrumpRx is already putting hundreds of millions back in patients’ pockets.

The platform has delivered more than $700 million in savings and now covers more than 1,000 branded and generic medicines. GLP-1 drugs that once cost over $1,000 a month start as low as $149; eligible Medicare seniors pay just $50 a month, with more than 500,000 seniors already saving $216 million. Fertility drugs, inhalers, insulin, cholesterol treatments, and dozens of other high-cost drugs have been slashed 50–90% or more.

President Trump is bringing drug manufacturing home and securing our supply chain.

The same 26 companies have committed about $170 billion to U.S. manufacturing and R&D and are stocking the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve — cutting America’s dependence on foreign supply chains for essential medicines.

President Donald J. Trump is delivering on his promises to America’s outdoorsmen by cutting red tape, removing burdensome and unnecessary restrictions levied by previous Administrations and expanding America’s great outdoor recreation sector that generates over $1.2 trillion annually and supports over 5 million jobs. 

Last night, the President signed two Executive Orders to bolster American hunting and revive American saltwater angling. Industry leaders and stakeholders nationwide hailed the President’s  leadership and commitment to restoring Americans’ access to Federal lands, revitalizing our Nation’s outdoor recreation economy, while conserving and protecting America’s abundant natural resources. 

Here’s what they are saying: 

Secretary Doug Burgum: “Sportsmen are among our greatest conservationists, and this administration is committed to supporting the men and women who help protect our public lands and wildlife.  At @POTUS’ direction, @Interior will: 

  • Expand hunting access
  • Promote habitat management
  • Improve migratory bird hunting authorizations
  • Encourage Sunday hunting
  • Support hunter education and youth and veteran programs

Putting American hunters, fishermen and outdoorsmen FIRST.”

Senator Tom Cotton: “Hunting is an important part of Arkansas’s culture and economy. Thankful President Trump is prioritizing America’s hunting heritage for future generations.”

Rep. Bruce Westerman: “Today’s executive orders signed by President Trump are generational victories for America’s sportsmen and women. The actions taken by President Trump expand access to public lands and waters, eliminate burdensome regulation, reinvigorate our outdoor economy and invest in the next generation of hunters and anglers. I’m proud to have advanced legislation on many of these policies through the Natural Resources Committee, including the reauthorization of the Great American Outdoors Act. I look forward to working with the Trump administration to codify these executive orders and support our nation’s hunters and anglers.”

Rep. August Pfluger: “For years, Washington made it harder to access the public lands and waters that belong to the American people. Today’s executive order by @POTUS expands wildlife access to hunters and anglers, rolls back overreaching Biden-era restrictions like the lead ammunition mandates, and opens up more opportunities for the next generation of sportsmen. I’m proud to support this action and applaud President Trump for rolling back the overreach of the previous administration.”

Rep. Addison McDowell: “Proud to join hundreds of anglers and hunters tonight as President Trump just signed an executive order reversing Biden-era restrictions on America’s outdoorsmen. By cutting burdensome red tape on fishermen and bringing outdoor recreation into the 21st century, President Trump is putting the American Outdoorsman First!”

The National Rifle Association: “The NRA is proud to stand beside @POTUS to protect the Second Amendment nationwide. We applaud President Trump’s newest executive orders protecting the storied tradition of American outdoorsmanship. 🤝”

Center for Sportfish Policy President and CEO Jeff Angers: “This Executive Order is a historic recognition of what millions of American anglers and coastal communities have known for decades: marine recreational fishing deserves a management system built for the way Americans fish. By prioritizing better data, stronger state partnerships and modern management approaches, President Trump’s order builds on our conservation gains creating a path to more reliable access and opportunity in America’s oceans.”

National Shooting Sports Foundation President and CEO Joe Bartozzi: “Today’s Executive Order by President Trump demonstrates that this administration stands with America’s sportsmen and women. This is a tremendous victory to ensure that America’s hunting heritage is protected for today’s hunters and the coming generations of outdoorsmen and women. NSSF has long championed several of these key policy issues, including protecting the right to use traditional ammunition, accessing public lands and increasing opportunities for Sunday hunting. We are proud to have led this fight and prouder still that the Trump administration is embracing commonsense policies to promote, protect and preserve hunting and the shooting sports across America.”

Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation President and CEO Jeff Crane: “The Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation commends President Trump for bringing together leaders from across the sportsmen’s community and recognizing the tremendous contributions hunters, anglers, trappers, and recreational shooters make to our nation. America’s outdoor heritage is one of our nation’s greatest traditions, and today’s event demonstrates the President’s continued commitment to ensuring these traditions remain strong for generations to come.”

Ducks Unlimited CEO Adam Putnam: “Hunters have been our nation’s most ardent conservationists for generations, and it’s terrific to see President Trump publicly recognize that in the White House Rose Garden. This Executive Order is an acknowledgment of hunters’ longstanding contributions to conservation, hunting access, sound waterfowl science, and hunter education. Our proud hunting heritage has been woven into the fabric of our great nation’s identity for 250 years, and this sort of commitment will help ensure it remains that way for future generations.”

Delta Waterfowl CEO Jason Tharpe: “We sincerely appreciate the President’s Executive Order as it highlights a number of Delta’s priorities for both ducks and duck hunters. Having the President affirm the need for access, addressing infrastructure on public lands, enhancing habitat through agreements with willing landowners and ensuring waterfowl hunting regulations are based on the best available data are all core needs and we appreciate the President’s leadership. Delta Waterfowl is deeply appreciative of President Trump’s historic announcement in furtherance of America’s hunting and conservation heritage. Simply put, this executive order will serve to benefit ducks and duck hunters for years to come and we look forward to working closely with the administration toward its implementation.” 

National Marine Manufacturers Association President and CEO Frank Hugelmeyer: “Recreational boating and fishing are the foundation of America’s outdoor heritage and an important driver of our nation’s recreation economy. [Yesterday’s] actions further reaffirm the importance of ensuring Americans can access and enjoy our nation’s waters. Access supports American manufacturing, jobs, and small businesses across the country. Thank you to President Trump and his administration for recognizing the value of outdoor recreation and the American industries and communities it supports.”

Coastal Conservation Association President and CEO Pat Murray: “We’re grateful the Administration has taken this opportunity to emphasize the social and economic importance of recreational fishing. State-based management has never been more important for our federal fisheries and we applaud this critical need being highlighted in this Executive Order.”

American Sportfishing Association President and CEO Glenn Hughes: “The American Sportfishing Association thanks President Trump for this decisive action to improve management and data collection for America’s saltwater fisheries. This Executive Order will have long-term benefits for the sportfishing industry and America’s 15.5 million saltwater recreational anglers.” 

Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation President and CEO Kyle Weaver: “On behalf of the Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation (RMEF), we thank President Trump and his administration for recognizing the vital role hunters play in sustaining wildlife and for issuing the Reinvigorating America’s Hunting Heritage Executive Order that strongly aligns with RMEF’s mission to ensure the future of elk, other wildlife, their habitat and our hunting heritage. We are honored by the president’s invitation to attend the White House ceremony where the policy was announced.

The order’s focus on expanding public access, actively managing habitat, facilitating wildlife movement and habitat connectivity, strengthening cooperation with state wildlife agencies, supporting science-based management of game populations, addressing predators and other population-limiting factors, and combatting invasive species closely reflects RMEF’s work for more than four decades. These priorities are central to our mission, and we look forward to working with the administration, federal agencies and state partners as the order is implemented.”

Sportsman Boats CEO Tommy Hancock: “Healthy fisheries and access to them go hand in hand. For American boat builders, this is about more than the boats we build. It’s about the families who spend time together on the water, the men and women whose livelihoods depend on the marine industry and our shared responsibility to conserve these resources. We appreciate President Trump and his Administration recognizing the importance of recreational fishing and taking action to strengthen conservation, improve fisheries management and preserve meaningful access.”

Rivers of Recovery Chairman Mitch Butler: “Rivers of Recovery commends the Trump Administration for recognizing the importance of America’s hunting and fishing traditions and expanding access to these opportunities for our nation’s veterans. Our years of research have proven that intentionally designed outdoor experiences can produce measurable improvements in the well being of combat veterans, including reductions in symptoms of post traumatic stress, depression and anxiety. By strengthening access to hunting, fishing and the outdoors, this action supports both the healing of our nation’s veterans and the conservation heritage that makes these experiences possible.” 

Pheasants Forever and Quail Forever Vice President of Government Affairs Ariel Wiegard: “America’s hunting heritage is worth protecting—and that starts with putting more wildlife on the landscape and more opportunity within reach of hunters. From expanding access to public lands to investing in the habitat, wildlife management, and community spirit needed to sustain the legacy of iconic game species like bobwhite quail, this Executive Order recognizes that conservation and hunting go hand in hand. Pheasants Forever and Quail Forever are proud to work alongside the Trump Administration, states, landowners, and hunters to ensure America’s hunting traditions remain strong for generations to come.”

Mule Deer Foundation President and CEO Greg Sheehan: “Growing mule deer and other game populations requires healthy habitat and strong partnerships. We appreciate President Trump and his Administration’s focus on working with states, landowners, and conservation partners to address the factors limiting these herds. The Mule Deer Foundation stands ready to help deliver measurable conservation results.”

American Association of Meat Processors Executive Director Chris Young: “The American Association of Meat Processors is proud to support the President’s Hunter’s Bill of Rights. We are particularly excited about the effort to expand wild game donation programs across the United States and our members, the small meat processors of the country who butcher the vast majority of the wild game meat, stand ready to help keep this promise to the American people.”

National Deer Association President and CEO Nick Pinizzotto: “The National Deer Association is proud to celebrate the announcement of a Hunter’s Bill of Rights, especially the President’s keen attention to the issue of venison donation. There are so many places in this country that are experiencing hyperabundant deer populations. Venison donation programs are good for hunters, good for agricultural producers, and good for our small business partners in the meat processing community. We are excited to continue our work on this issue as hunting seasons start to open across the country”

Wild Sheep Foundation CEO Gray Thornton: “The Wild Sheep Foundation applauds the administration’s continued emphasis on hunting access, voluntary work with landowners, and care for public lands as vital parts of wildlife conservation.  The Castle Mountains National Monument was wrongly closed to hunters and now we can look forward to correcting that error.”

Boone and Crockett Club CEO Tony Schoonen: “As fall hunting seasons begin across the country, the Boone and Crockett Club appreciates the administration’s timely attention to the important issues facing wildlife today.  We look forward to working with the now mobilized agencies to address today’s challenges with quail, bighorn sheep, mule deer, and other species not yet fully recovered.”

American Conservation Coalition President Chris Barnard: “Hunting and fishing are ingrained in the DNA of our nation and serve as crucial tools for the conservation of our natural heritage. The American Conservation Coalition and our 150,000 grassroots members are glad to see the administration’s efforts to expand access and continue this American tradition in balance with our conservation needs.” 

Contender Boats CEO Joe Neber: “The future of recreational fishing depends on healthy oceans and healthy fisheries. Anglers have long understood that good conservation and good access are connected. By putting better science, modern technology and more effective management at the center of federal fisheries policy, this Executive Order provides a stronger foundation for both.”
